# Sanika Mhatre | Portfolio

A responsive, static portfolio based on `Sanika_Resume_Nov_26.pdf`. No framework, package installation, or build step is required.

## Preview

Open `index.html` in a browser. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts and icons from the pinned Lucide CDN; an internet connection is needed for those enhancements. Content, project diagrams, and navigation are local.

## Publish on GitHub Pages

1. Add these files to the root of your GitHub repository, keeping the `assets` folder and resume PDF.
2. In the repository's **Settings > Pages**, choose **Deploy from a branch**.
3. Select your publishing branch and **/ (root)**, then save.

For a user site, the repository must match the GitHub account: `SanikaMhatre.github.io` for the resume's `SanikaMhatre` account. Other repository names publish under a project path. All local links are relative to support either option.

## Edit

- `index.html`: biography, experience, projects, contact links, and resume link.
- `styles.css`: colors, typography, spacing, and responsive layouts.
- `script.js`: navigation section highlighting, current year, and icons.
- `assets/`: original explanatory architecture diagrams, not clinical results or actual model predictions.

Experience dates, metrics, education, and links come from the supplied resume. The introductory biography is an initial editorial draft for review. No unpublished implementation details or seniority claims have been added.

The site has no tracking, contact-form backend, or deployment automation. Email links open the visitor's email application.

## Preview

Open `index.html` in a browser. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts and icons from the pinned Lucide CDN; an internet connection is needed for those enhancements. Content, project diagrams, and navigation are local.

## Publish on GitHub Pages

1. Add these files to the root of your GitHub repository, keeping the `assets` folder and resume PDF.
2. In the repository's **Settings > Pages**, choose **Deploy from a branch**.
3. Select your publishing branch and **/ (root)**, then save.

For a user site, the repository must match the GitHub account: `SanikaMhatre.github.io` for the resume's `SanikaMhatre` account. Other repository names publish under a project path. All local links are relative to support either option.

## Edit

- `index.html`: biography, experience, projects, contact links, and resume link.
- `styles.css`: colors, typography, spacing, and responsive layouts.
- `script.js`: navigation section highlighting, current year, and icons.
- `assets/`: original explanatory architecture diagrams, not clinical results or actual model predictions.

Experience dates, metrics, and education come from the supplied resume. The P&ID Digitizer and VoiceStack project summaries also draw from their public repository READMEs. Run every command in a terminal opened inside the project folder. The tests and the offline mode need no API key; the smoke tests, the live
evaluation and the live UI call Meta's models and do.


1. Requirements: Python 3.10 or newer (conda or venv), and a Meta Model API account at [dev.meta.ai](https://dev.meta.ai/) with credits.


2. Create an environment and install

  conda create -n pid python=3.12 -y     # or: python -m venv .venv  and activate it
conda activate pid
pip install -e ".[dev]"                # installs the project and its dependencies from pyproject.toml, plus pytest
pytest -q                              # every test should pass (no API key needed for this)
3. Get an API key


1. Sign in at [dev.meta.ai](https://dev.meta.ai/) and click API keys in the left menu.

2. Click Create API key, name it (for example `pid-digitizer`) and copy it right away. It is shown only once.
3. Open Billing or Usage to confirm your credits are on the account.


4. Create `.env`

  copy .env.example .env                 # Windows
cp .env.example .env                   # Mac / Linux
Open `.env` in a text editor and fill in these three lines (only the key changes):

  
```
LLM_API_KEY=paste-your-key-here
LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai/v1
LLM_MODEL=muse-spark-1.3

```

• The program reads `.env` automatically from the folder you run commands in. You do not need to export
variables.
• The file must be named exactly `.env` (not `.env.txt`; Windows can hide extensions). Check with `dir .env*`.
• Use the Standard model, not `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`: Contributor mode lets Meta train on your inputs.

## Architecture

Permalink: Architecture [Image: Image]


Blue stages call a Meta model; the others are ordinary code. Only the rule
engine decides violations.


Example graph. A net records which side of each symbol it touches, so flow direction and
junctions are kept.

 [Image: Image]


Verification agent. It can call only four whitelisted tools, every call is logged, and unresolved
items go to a person.

 [Image: Image]


Why nets, not edges. A tee feeding two valves is one net with three attachments, not a clique of
edges. Flow direction comes from the side a pipe meets a symbol (west = inlet, east
= outlet), which is what lets rules say "downstream of the pump".

## Rules

Permalink: Rules
Rules are YAML. Example:

  - id: R4-PUMP-CHECK-VALVE
  severity: warning
  description: Pump discharge needs a check valve within 2 hops downstream
  applies_to: {class: pump}
  require:
    path: {direction: downstream, edge_type: process, max_hops: 2, reaches: {class:
check_valve}}
Requirements: `path`, `unique: tag`, `has_attr: tag`, `connected: true`, and `min_symbols: N` (for `kind: net`). The starter pack (`src/pid/rules/starter_pack.yaml`) is illustrative: real plants apply their own engineering standards, and passing these checks
does not establish safety compliance.


Natural-language rules ("every pump needs an isolation valve on both sides") are
compiled by the Muse model into this DSL, validated against the schema (unknown classes and malformed conditions are rejected and sent back for
repair), previewed on reference sheets, and applied only after you approve them.

## Evaluation protocol

Permalink: Evaluation protocol
• Sheets are generated by `pid.synth` (original symbols, so there are no data-rights issues) with planted errors; the
expected violations are known by construction. Seeds < 1000 are development, ≥
1000 are held-out test.
• Metrics: symbol localization/class F1 (IoU 0.5), tag read accuracy, connectivity
F1 on (symbol pair, net type), violation F1 against the violations the engine
raises on the ground-truth graph, planted-error recall, seconds and dollars per
sheet, items sent to review.
• `--mode simulated` replaces the model stages with ground-truth lookups, so it scores tracing,
rules and metrics only; it is not a measure of model accuracy.
• Public P&ID datasets (e.g. the PID2Graph benchmark) can be added for
real-drawing evaluation; check their licenses first and adapt a loader to `pid.schema.Graph`. None are bundled.

## Security and privacy

Permalink: Security and privacy
• Prompt injection: drawings can contain arbitrary text. Model outputs are schema-constrained,
agent tools are a closed whitelist with validated arguments, and nothing a model
returns is executed or used as a rule verdict. The worst a hostile tag can do is
produce a wrong tag value, which lands in the review queue when confidence is low.
• Confidential drawings: use the Standard model (not the `-contributor` one, which lets Meta train on inputs). Muse Spark Open's weights are
downloadable, so the model stages can also run on infrastructure you control. Responses
are cached on disk (`PID_CACHE_DIR`), keyed by a hash of the request; delete `.cache/` to purge. Request bodies containing images are not written to logs.
• API: upload size and pixel limits, optional bearer-token auth (`PID_API_KEY`, constant-time compare), request ids, no upstream error details returned to
clients, non-root container.
• Secrets: read from the environment only; `.env` is git-ignored.

# P&ID Digitizer

## Limitations (known, deliberate)

Permalink: Limitations (known, deliberate)
• Line crossings vs junctions cannot be distinguished by pixel connectivity; both merge. Drawings with
crossings need jump symbols or a dedicated check (the agent can flag them; not
implemented).
• Tag text that touches a pipe is treated as part of the pipe.
• Flow direction assumes west-to-east conventions; drawings with other layouts
need the attachment-side convention generalized.
• One sheet at a time: off-page connectors and multi-sheet consistency are not
implemented.
• Pipe sizes, line numbers and specifications are not read.
• The generator's drawing style is simple; real scans will be harder.

# P&ID Digitizer

Permalink: P&ID Digitizer
Scanned engineering drawing in → verified graph, bill of materials and
design-rule violations out.


Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon (Push the Frontier:
manufacturing and energy). Built with Meta models: SAM 3.1 finds the symbols, a Muse model reads them and verifies uncertain ones.
Both are called through the Meta Model API.


Process plants hold decades of drawings as images. Their structure (which pump
feeds which vessel, which valves isolate what) is locked in pixels, which blocks
plant modifications, safety reviews and digital twins. This project reads a P&ID
and produces:


1. a machine-readable graph (symbols, tags, and the pipes / signal lines connecting them)
2. a bill of materials (CSV)
3. an annotated overlay of the original drawing
4. design-rule violations, each pointing at the exact place on the drawing; new rules can be written in
plain English

>

# P&ID Digitizer
...
Design principle: models propose, deterministic code decides. SAM 3.1 and the Muse model produce candidate symbols, tags and links with
confidences. A verification agent re-examines the uncertain ones with tools. The rule
engine that raises violations is ordinary code over the graph, so every finding
is reproducible, testable and auditable. A language model can author a rule, but it can never decide whether a rule is violated.

## Features

Permalink: Features
• MCP server over Streamable HTTP (spec 2025-11-25) at `/mcp`, with eight tools.
• No double-booking: a database constraint plus transactions; 20 simultaneous requests for one slot
produce exactly one winner.
• Safe retries: `confirm_booking` accepts an `idempotency_key`, so a repeated call returns the same booking.
• Two-minute holds that expire on their own, then free the slot.
• Waitlist: when a booking is cancelled, the longest-waiting customer is offered the slot.
• Owner approval: a shop is bookable only after the owner approves the draft with a code.
• Audit log per shop, including refused attempts.
• Hindi and English: Devanagari and Roman Hindi, rule-based, no language model.
• Demo page with three views: Customer, Shop owner, Developer.

## How it stays correct

Permalink: How it stays correct
• A primary key on `occupancy(business_id, resource_id, start)` inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions prevents two bookings for one slot.
• Hold expiry is checked in code against the clock.
• `confirm_booking` stores each `(operation, key)` with a request fingerprint; reusing a key for a different hold is rejected.
• Prices are integer paise; all times are Asia/Kolkata.
• No language model writes to the database.

 
## Security

Permalink: Security
One middleware (`voicestack/security.py`) covers every route: host and origin allow-list, rate limit, 1 MiB body cap,
security headers, a structured access log with request ids that never contains
request bodies or customer names, and a lock after five wrong approval codes.
Health probes: `/api/health`, `/api/ready`. Settings are listed in the technical documentation, section 15.2.

## Limitations

Permalink: Limitations
• Not tested on a real Alexa+ device. The demo page is an MCP client with typed or
browser-recognised speech standing in for Alexa+.
• No authentication or account linking; every tool and route is public. Anyone
holding a `booking_id` or `hold_id` can act on it. A real deployment would add OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.
• `/api/day` and `/api/audit` are unauthenticated, and `/api/seed` (demo only) skips owner approval. Do not use real customer data.
• The parser is rule-based: common Hindi (Devanagari and Roman) and English
phrases and a built-in list of service words, not free-form language. "kal" is always
read as tomorrow.
• One timezone (Asia/Kolkata), 30-minute booking blocks, no payments.
• Waitlist: if an offer expires unclaimed, the slot becomes free again and is not
passed to the next waiter.

01 / SELECTED WORK

Built with purpose.

All repositories
PROJECT / 01
Kidney Tumor Segmentation
Finding the small details that matter. A double U-Net++ with an EfficientNet-B1 backbone for small tumor localization and precise lesion boundaries.
PROJECT / 02
Clinical RAG Assistant
Clinical knowledge, grounded in the source. Hybrid retrieval and cross-encoder reranking with PII redaction, conversational memory, and independent LLM evaluation.
PROJECT / 03
P&ID Digitizer

From scanned engineering drawings to structured graphs, bills of materials, and design-rule findings. SAM 3.1 locates symbols; Muse reads them, an agent reviews uncertainty, and deterministic code checks the rules. Evaluated on generated sheets, not plant safety compliance.
PROJECT / 04

A self-hosted booking backend for local businesses, with Hindi/English input, expiring slot holds, waitlists, and retry-safe confirmations. SQLite transactions prevent double-booking. A browser demo with rule-based parsing, no LLM, and no real-device Alexa+ validation.

02 / EXPERIENCE

Research meets execution.

Across AI, healthcare & cloud

AI & Data Science Intern

Built reusable ML infrastructure and applied AI systems, from distributed training to clinical imaging and enterprise knowledge retrieval.

  • Reusable MLOps / LLMOps pipelines for distributed GPU training, evaluation, versioning, and lifecycle automation.
  • Classical ML and 2D / 3D deep learning on 10,000+ DICOM images, with explainability for clinical validation.
  • GenAI, agentic AI, and RAG pipelines for grounded natural-language querying over enterprise data.
  • Real-time analytics with 4 KPI categories, 12 interactive visualizations, and automated reporting.

Trainee Cloud Engineer

01 / SELECTED WORK

Built with purpose.

All repositories
PROJECT / 01
Kidney Tumor Segmentation
Finding the small details that matter. A double U-Net++ with an EfficientNet-B1 backbone for small tumor localization and precise lesion boundaries.
PROJECT / 02
Clinical RAG Assistant
Clinical knowledge, grounded in the source. Hybrid retrieval and cross-encoder reranking with PII redaction, conversational memory, and independent LLM evaluation.
PROJECT / 03
P&ID Digitizer

From scanned engineering drawings to structured graphs, bills of materials, and design-rule findings. SAM 3.1 locates symbols; Muse reads them, an agent reviews uncertainty, and deterministic code checks the rules. Evaluated on generated sheets, not plant safety compliance.
PROJECT / 04

A self-hosted booking backend for local businesses, with Hindi/English input, expiring slot holds, waitlists, and retry-safe confirmations. SQLite transactions prevent double-booking. A browser demo with rule-based parsing, no LLM, and no real-device Alexa+ validation.

02 / EXPERIENCE

Research meets execution.

Across AI, healthcare & cloud

AI & Data Science Intern

Built reusable ML infrastructure and applied AI systems, from distributed training to clinical imaging and enterprise knowledge retrieval.

  • Reusable MLOps / LLMOps pipelines for distributed GPU training, evaluation, versioning, and lifecycle automation.
  • Classical ML and 2D / 3D deep learning on 10,000+ DICOM images, with explainability for clinical validation.
  • GenAI, agentic AI, and RAG pipelines for grounded natural-language querying over enterprise data.
  • Real-time analytics with 4 KPI categories, 12 interactive visualizations, and automated reporting.
80%less manual orchestration
70%less lookup time
60%less manual reporting

# Define Double U-Net Model
class
DoubleUNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, enc_name='efficientnet-b1', classes=2,
pretrain='imagenet'):
        super(DoubleUNet, self).__init__()
       
       
self.unet_plus = smp.UnetPlusPlus(
            encoder_name=enc_name,
         
  encoder_weights=pretrain,
            in_channels=1,
           
classes=classes,
        )
       
        self.unet = smp.Unet(
           
encoder_name=enc_name,
            encoder_weights=pretrain,
            in_channels=1,
       
    classes=classes,
        )
       
        self.final_conv =
nn.Conv2d(classes * 2, classes, kernel_size=1)
   
    def forward(self, x):
        out1 =
self.unet_plus(x)
        out2 = self.unet(x)
        out = torch.cat((out1,
out2), dim=1)
        return self.final_conv(out)

class Evaluator:
    def __init__(self, num_classes):
        self.num_classes =
num_classes
        self.confusion_matrix = np.zeros((num_classes, num_classes))
  
 
    def add(self, pred, target):
        # Flatten the arrays
        pred =
pred.reshape(-1)
        target = target.reshape(-1)
        
        #
Accumulate confusion matrix
        mask = (target >= 0) & (target < self.num_classes)
 
      if mask.sum() > 0:
            hist = np.bincount(
               
self.num_classes * target[mask].astype(int) + pred[mask],
               
minlength=self.num_classes ** 2).reshape(self.num_classes, self.num_classes)
           
self.confusion_matrix += hist
    
    def reset(self):
       
self.confusion_matrix = np.zeros((self.num_classes, self.num_classes))
    
    def
pixel_accuracy(self):
        acc = np.diag(self.confusion_matrix).sum() /
self.confusion_matrix.sum()
        return acc
